name: Cotoxo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page coto1237 'Cotoxo' (refs: Silva Martins 2007, von Martius 1867, Loukotka 1932).
sources.note: Bibliographic record only; all three cited works were opened (above).

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1932. La familia lingüística Kamakan del Brasil. Revista del Instituto de Etnología de la Universidad Nacional de Tucumán 2: 493-524.
sources.note: Source list p. 496: 'Ko.: Kotošo. Martius... páginas 156-158'; 'Mo1.: Mongoyo. Wied zu Neuwied... t. II, páginas 327-330'. 'Fonética' p. 498 gives only the notational remark that accented vowels are marked with an accent. No stress position stated. (PDF../kama1372/.)

sources.citation: Etnolinguistica.org catalogue page 'Kamakã †' (no separate Kotoxó/Mongoyó page; lingua:kotoxo and lingua:mongoyo return 404).
sources.note: Bibliography only: Étienne 1912, Oliveira 1892, Loukotka 1932, Nimuendajú 1986, Ploetz & Métraux 1930, Métraux & Nimuendajú 1946, Grahl 2009, Wied-Neuwied 1942/1989, Nimuendajú & Guérios 1948, Martins 2007/2009, Ribeiro 2009. No additional Kotoxó source.

sources.citation: Nikulin, Andrey. 2020. Proto-Macro-Jê: um estudo reconstrutivo. PhD thesis, Universidade de Brasília. 595 pp.
sources.note: p. 23: for Kotoxó/Mongoyó[coto1237] the only data are Wied-Neuwied ([1820] 1940: 491-493, as Camacan/Mongoió) and Martius (1867 v. 2: 156-158, as Kotoxó); the Kamakã family is not treated phonologically ('Não abordaremos a família Kamakã'). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Ramirez, Henri, Valdir Vegini & Maria Cristina Victorino de França. 2015. Koropó, puri, kamakã e outras línguas do Leste brasileiro: revisão e proposta de nova classificação. LIAMES 15(2): 223-277. doi:10.20396/liames.v15i2.8642302.
sources.note: Kamakã family pp. 249-251 (Kotoxó data = Martius 1863: 156-158; Mongoyó = Wied-Neuwied 1989: 514-516) and Anexo III wordlist pp. 269 ff.; argues Kamakã/Kotoxó/Mongoyó/Katatoi were one language. p. 237: 'O uso de acentos e outros diacríticos... não vem acompanhado da devida explicação sobre os seus significados' (of the old lists). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Martins, Andérbio Márcio Silva. 2007. Revisão da família lingüística Kamakã proposta por Chestmir Loukotka. MA thesis, Universidade de Brasília. 89 pp.
sources.note: Section 3.2 (pp. 23-26) compares Wied's Mongoyó and Martius's Kotoxó lists, finds <10% mismatch, and unites them as one language 'Kotoxó'; ch. 3 (pp. 20-21) discusses only the segmental spelling habits of Martius/Wied (aspiration, ä/ö/ü). No occurrence of 'acento'/'tônica'; silent on stress.

sources.citation: Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp von. 1863. Glossaria linguarum Brasiliensium. Glossarios de diversas lingoas e dialectos, que fallao os Indios no imperio do Brazil. Wörtersammlung brasilianischer Sprachen. Erlangen: Junge (= Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens II, Leipzig 1867). Cotoxó wordlist pp. 156-158.
sources.note: Latin-Cotoxó wordlist pp. 156-158 (PDF pp. 183-185; page images verified) taken at S. Pedro d'Alcantara from one speaker who called himself Cotoxó, supplemented with Wied's Mongoyó forms marked N. Only the general orthographic key p. 29 (written about Tupi, applied to the whole book): the acute (') 'dient, den Vocal zu schärfen oder die Sylbe zu betonen'. No Cotoxó stress statement. (1867 reissue scanned also saved:, identical pages.)

sources.citation: Wied-Neuwied, Maximilian Prinz zu. 1821. Reise nach Brasilien in den Jahren 1815 bis 1817, Bd. 2. Frankfurt a. M.: Brönner. '7) Sprachproben der Camacans oder Mongoyóz in der Capitania da Bahia', pp. 327-330.
sources.note: Anmerkung p. 327 (PDF p. 365, page image verified): strange language with many gutturals; 'Die Worte werden am Ende auf eine sonderbare Art abgekürzt ausgesprochen... a und o sind die gewöhnlichen Endungen der Worte, werden aber äusserst kurz abgebrochen, als wenn der Sprecher hier plötzlich den Ton aufhielte'. Only per-word accent remarks: 'Kediahaie (e k., hai der Accent)', 'Hohion (... ohne besonderen Accent)', 'Niukuá (niu kaum hörbar, kuá laut mit Accent)', 'Hoihi (ki Accent)', 'Koinin (nin der Accent)', 'Hüdiä (k., Accent auf diä)', 'Ake (e k. und mit Accent)', 'Peo (o voll, Accent auf…

sources.citation: Ribeiro, Eduardo Rivail. 2009. Old data, new cognates: the case of the 'marker of alienable possession' in the Kamakã, Purí, and Krenák families. In Braggio & Martins Filho (eds.), Línguas e culturas Macro-Jê. Goiânia: Vieira.

sources.note: Comparative morphology using the same wordlists; listed on etnolinguistica.org's Kamakã page; very unlikely to state stress but is the remaining unread family item.

sources.citation: Guérios, R. F. Mansur. 1945. Estudos sôbre a língua Camacã: pequeno vocabulário, notas gramaticais, investigações etimológicas. Arquivos do Museu Paranaense 4: 291-320.

sources.note: Only 20th-century first-hand record of the family (Kamakã proper, kama1372) with an explicit accent key (acute on last syllable = tonic, otherwise paroxytone, as quoted by Grahl 2009: 59-60); relevant here only if one accepts Ramirez et al. 2015 that Kamakã and Kotoxó/Mongoyó are one language.

sources.citation: Wied-Neuwied, Maximiliano. 1940 [1989]. Viagem ao Brasil (trans. E. S. de Mendonça & F. P. de Figueiredo). São Paulo: Companhia Editora Nacional (Brasiliana 1); reissued Belo Horizonte: Itatiaia, 1989. Mongoyó list pp. 491-493 (1940) / 514-516 (1989).

sources.citation: Métraux, Alfred. 1930. Les Indiens Kamakan, Pataso et Kutaso d'après le journal de route inédit de l'explorateur français J. B. Douville. Revista del Instituto de Etnología de la Universidad Nacional de Tucumán 1: 239-294.

sources.note: Publishes Douville's 1833-35 Kamakã vocabulary and phrases and Kutaxó (= Kotoxó per Loukotka 1932: 497) ethnography; the only other early record from the same region, could carry pronunciation remarks. Not found on archive.org or etnolinguistica.org.
